items.title: A mole of marshmallows would cover the USA 600 miles deep
items.claim: 6.022 times 10 to the 23 is just a number until you try to picture it. Avogadro's number of marshmallows would bury the entire surface of the United States to a depth of 600 miles.
items.prompt: Roughly how many moles of water molecules are in a single drop (about 0.05 mL)?

options.text: About 0.003 moles, which is roughly 1.7 times 10 to the 21 molecules
Around 6 times 10 to the 23 — one drop is one mole
About 0.05 moles, the same as the volume in millilitres

items.reveal_title: Even a microscopic drop contains stupefying numbers of molecules
items.reveal:
0.05 mL of water has a mass of 0.05 g. Water is 18 g per mole, so 0.05 / 18 equals about 0.0028 mol. Multiply by Avogadro's number and you get roughly 1.7 times 10 to the 21 molecules.

If you counted those molecules at one per second, it would take about 50 trillion years — over 3000 times the age of the universe. Chemistry is the study of mind-bending counts of incredibly tiny things.
items.why: The mole is treated as a unit conversion when it should be treated as a stark statement about scale.

items.title: Strong and concentrated are completely different
items.claim: A 0.0001 M solution of hydrochloric acid is a strong acid but dilute. A 12 M solution of ethanoic acid is concentrated but weak. Strength and concentration are independent properties of an acid.
items.prompt: What does 'strong' actually mean for an acid?

options.text: It feels acidic on the tongue
It is fully dissociated into ions in water (Ka very large); concentration is just how much acid is dissolved per unit volume
It is sold in glass bottles

items.reveal:
Strong acids — HCl, HBr, HI, HNO3, H2SO4, HClO4 — dissociate essentially 100 percent in water. [H+] equals the acid concentration.

Weak acids — CH3COOH, HCN, H2CO3, HF — only partially dissociate. Vinegar is about 1 M ethanoic acid but [H+] is only about 0.004 M; most molecules stay intact.

Very dilute HCl is still strong (fully dissociated) but has a low [H+] and a high pH near 7. Glacial ethanoic acid is very concentrated but most molecules are undissociated — pH only modestly below 7 until water is added.

pKa describes strength; molarity describes concentration. They are independent properties.
items.why: Strength and concentration are routinely conflated. They measure entirely different physical properties of an acid.

items.title: Rubber heats up when stretched, cools when relaxed
items.claim: Stretch a rubber band quickly and press it to your lip — it feels warm. Let it snap back and it feels cool. Stretching does work ON the rubber, but the rubber gives heat OUT.
items.prompt: Why does stretching rubber release heat?

options.text: Stretching aligns the polymer chains, dramatically reducing entropy — the system must release heat to keep delta G zero at constant T and constant tension
The rubber band's atoms vibrate faster when stretched
The rubber compresses internally as you stretch it externally

items.reveal:
Most materials store elastic energy in bond stretching (enthalpy). Rubber stores almost no energy in bonds — its restoring force comes from entropy.

Unstretched rubber chains are tangled and random (high entropy). Stretching forces them into more aligned configurations (lower entropy). To keep free energy minimised at constant temperature, the system releases heat to the surroundings.

The consequence (Gough-Joule effect): a stretched rubber band CONTRACTS when heated, the opposite of steel. Heat the band and you increase tension on its disordered state — pulling it more tightly random.
items.why: Most students associate stretching with stored energy in bonds. Rubber's elasticity is statistical mechanics, not chemistry.
